report.value: TLV7011 (-0.3 to 6 V) and TLV7031 (-0.3 to 7 V) clamp their inputs to VEE only and rate them independent of VCC. TLV1811 rates inputs to (V+) + 0.3 V. P2's three parts clamp to both rails (TLV3201 -0.5 V to VCC + 0.5 V, TLV3501 and TLV3601 -0.3 V to VCC + 0.3 V). With the rail down, a coasting motor's divided phase signal flows into the rail through the divider on TLV3201, TLV3501, TLV3601 and TLV1811, and into nothing on TLV7011 and TLV7031 up to 6 V and 7 V. Stage 2's divider sets the current in each case

FU-C1's adjudicator ruled on the same point for MAX999 and found no stated figure that separates the parts. P4 verifies the alternate against the pins and the delay; the bias offset waits for the divider

report.value: P3's missed function holds. P2's rank 1 meets the lead-length value (V222: 2 m, its capacitance outside the delay-variation node) only with a buffer between XOUT and the lead, and no function or part selects that buffer. ADXL316's output resistor is 27 to 37 kOhm. The buffer's own delay variation counts inside the 1.244 us share, of which ADXL316 at 100 pF uses 1.000 us, leaving 0.244 us. 2 m of cable of an unknown capacitance would add to the 100 pF node without the buffer. The owner decides whether R11 gains a function for the buffer; none is selected here

report.value: The accelerometer's delay variation of 1.000 us is the RFILT x C pole alone, as V225's derivation names. The sensor's own response, 1,600 Hz bandwidth typical with no external filter and 4.2 kHz resonance (ADXL316), has no stated minimum or maximum and no phase at 1,092 Hz, so its delay variation at 1,092 Hz is not known. A single pole at 1,600 Hz would delay 1,092 Hz by about 87 us; the spread of that delay between parts is not stated
